topics.label: Introduction to the hallmarks of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture by outlining the learning objectives and introducing the hallmarks of cancer framework.

topics.label: Sustained proliferative signaling and growth factor independence
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how oncogenic mutations in pathways like Wnt/beta-catenin and receptor tyrosine kinases enable autonomous cancer cell proliferation.

topics.label: Differentiation block in cancer progression
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics demonstrate how impaired terminal differentiation maintains cells in a proliferative state in both leukemias and solid carcinomas.

topics.label: Evasion of programmed cell death
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details how cancer cells resist apoptosis through alterations in p53 regulation and the balance of Bcl-2 family proteins.

topics.label: Replicative immortality and cellular senescence
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the limits of normal cell division, the mechanisms of senescence, and how cancer cells activate telomerase to achieve immortality.

topics.label: Metabolic reprogramming and oncometabolites
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics investigate how cancer cells alter their metabolic pathways, including aerobic glycolysis and oncometabolite signaling, to sustain tumour growth.

topics.label: Induction of tumour angiogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the angiogenic switch and how tumours stimulate new blood vessel formation to overcome hypoxia and nutrient deprivation.

topics.label: Invasion and metastatic dissemination
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the multi-step cascade of cancer metastasis, including circulatory dissemination, seed-and-soil interactions, and associated genetic features.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and summary
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the concluding framing for the lecture, summarizing key takeaways and transitioning to practical sessions.
